pk.context: 40 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: opaque capsule with a green cap and an orange body (40 mg)

clues.kinetics: Food does not affect systemic bioavailability, though it may delay absorption by 1 to 2 hours. About 94.5% is protein bound, and hepatic metabolism to inactive metabolites is the main clearance route.
clues.substance: Supplied as the hydrochloride salt, molecular weight 345.79 against 309.33 for the free base. A racemic 50/50 mixture of two enantiomers, soluble to 14 mg/mL in water.
clues.product: Sold under an NDA in 10, 20 and 40 mg strengths, with a 60 mg strength also listed by FDA. A combination with olanzapine is covered by the same label.
clues.safety: Boxed warning for suicidal thoughts and behavior in children, adolescents and young adults. Contraindicated with MAOIs, pimozide and thioridazine; insomnia, nausea and abnormal dreams are common.
clues.indication: Major depressive disorder, obsessive compulsive disorder, bulimia nervosa and panic disorder, plus bipolar depression and resistant depression when combined with olanzapine.
clues.mechanism: Presumed to act by inhibiting neuronal uptake of serotonin in the central nervous system; the exact mechanism is unknown.

tell: A half-life of days rather than hours, with a long-lived active metabolite, marks the original SSRI.
